record.summary: Binding amendment to India's intermediary rules on 'synthetically generated information' (SGI): content artificially or algorithmically created or altered so that it appears real and depicts a person or event as indistinguishable from reality. Intermediaries offering SGI tools must use technical measures to block unlawful SGI, such as child sexual abuse material, non-consensual intimate imagery or deceptive depictions of real people or events, and must prominently label other SGI and embed permanent metadata or a unique identifier where feasible. Significant social media intermediaries must obtain and verify user declarations of SGI and label it.
record.notes: G.S.R. 120(E) of 10 February 2026 amends the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 (G.S.R. 139(E) of 25 February 2021); the amendment came into force on 20 February 2026. Besides the SGI provisions, it clarifies that removing or disabling access to information, including SGI, in compliance with the rules does not breach the safe-harbour conditions of section 79(2) of the IT Act; requires intermediaries to inform users at least every three months of the consequences of non-compliance, and those offering SGI tools to warn users of penalties for misuse; and shortens deadlines: removal on a court order or a government authority's reasoned intimation from 36 to 3 hours (rule 3(1)(d) as substituted by G.S.R. 775(E) of 22 October 2025, in force from 15 November 2025), removal of intimate or impersonating imagery on complaint from 24 to 2 hours, grievance resolution from 15 to 7 days, and certain removal requests from 72 to 36 hours. A draft of the SGI amendment was published for consultation on 22 October 2025. The rules follow MeitY's non-binding AI advisories to intermediaries of 1 March 2024, revised on 15 March 2024 to drop a prior-approval requirement for under-tested models. On 30 March 2026 MeitY released a further draft amendment to the IT Rules, open for comment until 16 April 2026, under which intermediaries would have to comply with MeitY's clarifications, advisories, orders, directions, standard operating procedures and guidelines on implementing the rules as part of their due diligence.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored: MeitY's consolidated text of the IT Rules 2021 'updated as on 10.02.2026' (meity.gov.in, copy of 16 Oct 2026; the archiver's retry on 18 Oct 2026 failed with a DNS error). Its footnotes attribute to G.S.R. 120(E) dated 10.02.2026 the SGI definition (rule 2(1)(wa)), rules 2(1A) and 2(1B), the user-information duties (rule 3(1)(c) to (cb)), the SGI due diligence (rule 3(3)), the SSMI declarations (rule 4(1A)) and the 3-hour, 2-hour, 7-day and 36-hour deadlines, and to G.S.R. 775(E) of 22.10.2025 (w.e.f. 15.11.2025) the substituted rule 3(1)(d). The amendment notification itself was not found on an official host. Its short title and its commencement clause ('They shall come into force on February 20, 2026', Notification No. G.S.R. 120(E)) are quoted from TeamLease RegTech's reproduction of the notification text (a commercial compliance database, secondary). The draft amendment of 30 March 2026 rests on a Khaitan & Co client note of 8 April 2026 (secondary). The consultation draft of 22 October 2025 and the March 2024 advisories rest on version 1's law-firm sources and on no stored file.

judgment.status_reasoning: G.S.R. 120(E) dated 10.02.2026; MeitY's consolidated text 'updated as on 10.02.2026' already incorporates every provision of it. The notification text, as reproduced by TeamLease RegTech (secondary), says 'They shall come into force on February 20, 2026'. 20 February 2026 is before today, 18 October 2026, and nothing stored shows the amendment repealed or stayed. In force.
judgment.scope_reasoning: A binding rule that regulates synthetic media (deepfakes) through labelling, provenance and blocking duties; in scope with no note.
judgment.title_reasoning: The stored official file is the consolidated principal rules, which cites the amendment only as G.S.R. 120(E) dated 10.02.2026; the short title 'Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026' is quoted from the secondary reproduction of the notification.

leads.title: Draft amendment to the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, released by MeitY on 30 March 2026 (proposed Second Amendment)
leads.note: Would make compliance with MeitY clarifications, advisories, orders, directions, SOPs and guidelines part of intermediaries' due diligence, and extend rules 15 and 16 to news content shared by users; consultation until 16 April 2026. Not in the register; an official copy on meity.gov.in was not found.
